
=================================================================
#68 Sungchung  (660)
Arc: The Fall of Euija · place: sabi · tone: tragic loyalty drama
Logline: Two armies are coming for the capital, one by sea and one over the hills. The markets already have a name for it.
=================================================================
[0] ¶ The war reaches Sabi the way bad news always does: through the fish market first.
[1] ¶ Two armies are coming for the capital, one by sea and one over the hills. The fishwives already have a name for it: the Chunchu Army. The king hears it from a maid, who heard it from a fishwife.
[2] ── SCENE: The Hall ──
[3] ¶ Euija holds court for the first time in three years. Half the benches are his sons. They watch him the way sons watch a father who has come home sober: politely, and counting the exits.
[4] King Euija: The boat for Gyebek. / I gave that order on a riverbank, soaking wet, in front of witnesses. / Where is he?
[5] Satek Chunbok: Your Majesty… as Your Majesty well knows, the winter crossings are— / And then the spring winds were—
[6] King Euija: The winds. A whole year of winds. / Chunbok. Do you take me for a fool, or for a drunk?
[7] Satek Chunbok: Majesty, by Onjo’s shrine, we have too few troops to send General Gyebek! / The Satek house lost its benches, not its levies. Better to wait for Lord Satek’s men…
[8] King Euija: **Who is the Eraha of this country?!** / **Buyeo Euija?** / **Or Minister Satek?** / **Send him NOW!**
[9] ¶ Chunbok bows very low, which is what he does instead of answering. A boat leaves for Tamla that afternoon. It is the fastest in the harbour. It is a year late.
[10] ── SCENE: The Letter ──
[11] ¶ That night the king does something he has not done in three years. He goes looking for a piece of paper.
[12] ¶ It is where he left it in the banquet hall, under a wine jar, with a red ring where the jar stood. The maids watch him lift the jar. Nobody giggles.
[13] The Court Maids: Majesty… that’s the councillor’s. / We didn’t throw it away. / We didn’t know if we were allowed to.
[14] King Euija: Read it to me. / My eyes are— just read it.
[15] The Court Maids: ‘A loyal servant does not forget his king even in death—’ / Majesty, then it’s a river and a pass. / ‘Do not let them cross Chimhyeon by land. Do not let their ships into Final Ford.’ / …Then just his name.
[16] King Euija: Chimhyeon. The soldiers call it Tanhyeon. / He told me the pass and the river three years ago. Starving. Through that wall. / And I put a jar on him.
[17] The Court Maids: Majesty—
[18] King Euija: Somebody else said this. Before him. Smiling at me, quoting sutras— / …Heungsu.
[19] ── SCENE: The Back of the Hall ──
[20] ¶ Next morning the provincial lords are summoned too, even the ones nobody has ever summoned.
[21] ¶ At the back of the hall, the lord of Bear Fortress says nothing. Ye Sikjin is doing the sum every provincial lord is doing. How many days from the river mouth to the capital? And how many from the capital to his own gate?
[22] King Euija: Lord Ye! Bear Fortress! Four generations and I never once asked you to court. My mistake. / How many men can you give me?
[23] Ye Sikjin: Your Majesty is generous to say so. / Bear Fortress will do exactly what is needed, Majesty. The number depends on the road.
[24] King Euija: Every number depends on the road. Give me one.
[25] Ye Sikjin: …As many as the road allows, Majesty.
[26] ¶ Euija laughs, because a king has to laugh at something before noon. Ye Sikjin bows exactly as low as the man beside him. That afternoon he rides home to Bear Fortress and opens a drawer.
[27] ¶ **One man might still know what to do. Euija sent him away too. Somebody ride. Now…!**
